prompt:
Solve the following problem as completely as you can.

<problem>
For a prime power $q$, let $v_q=q^2+q+1$. A perfect difference set modulo $v$ is a set $B\subset\mathbb Z$ of residues that are pairwise distinct mod $v$, such that every nonzero residue mod $v$ equals $b-b'$ for exactly one ordered pair $(b,b')$ with $b,b'\in B$. A finite Sidon set is a set of integers whose differences $a-a'$ with $a\neq a'$ are all distinct. (a) Does every $4$-element Sidon set $A\subset\mathbb N$ lie inside some perfect difference set modulo $v_q$, for some prime power $q$? (b) More strongly, for each such $A$, does $A$ lie inside a Singer difference set modulo $v_q$ for infinitely many primes $q$? If so, does the set of primes $q$ for which this happens have positive relative density among the primes?
</problem>

<finite_instance>

</finite_instance>

<required_candidate_format>

</required_candidate_format>

Return
- text: your full solution or best partial progress: definitions, the argument, and a clear final answer. If you cannot solve it, state exactly what you proved and what remains.
- claimed_status: "solved" only if you believe the problem (or, when given, the finite instance) is fully solved; "partial" for real progress; "unsolved" otherwise.
- candidate: if a finite instance is given, the object you propose, exactly in the required JSON shape; otherwise null.

structured_output.text:
Setup. A Singer set mod v_q=q^2+q+1 is D(θ,V)={i mod v : θ^i ∈ V}, θ primitive in F_{q^3}, V a 2-dim F_q-subspace. WLOG A={0<d_2<d_3<d_4}. Lemma 1: A lies in a Singer set mod v_q iff d_4<v_q and some primitive θ satisfies θ^{d_3},θ^{d_4} ∈ W=span(1,θ^{d_2}) (V must equal W since 1,θ^{d_2} are independent). Writing θ^3=e_1θ^2−e_2θ+e_3, these are two fixed weighted-homogeneous integer polynomial equations (Schur functions s_{(d_3−2,d_2−1,0)}, s_{(d_4−2,d_2−1,0)} in the conjugates), defining a finite scheme Z_A ⊂ P(1,2,3); so A has only O_A(1) embeddings per q, and an embedding needs a point with irreducible cubic and θ^{q−1} generating the norm-one torus Z/v_q. Non-Sidon sets are excluded because a repeated difference forces θ^m∈F_q.

(b) NO. For A={0,1,3,7}: θ^3∈W means θ^3=βθ+α; then θ^7=2αβθ^2+(β^3+α^2)θ+αβ^2, so θ^7∈W iff 2αβ=0. For odd q this forces θ^2∈F_q or θ^3∈F_q, contradicting primitivity; for q=2, 7≡0 mod 7. Hence {0,1,3,7} lies in a Singer difference set mod v_q for NO prime q: the set of primes is empty (not infinite, density 0).

(a) for this A: YES with q=8. In char 2 the condition is just Tr(θ)=0; over F_8 there are 21 irreducible trinomials x^3+βx+α (63 trace-zero elements outside F_8), at most 8 with α=N(θ)=θ^{73}=1, so ≥13 have θ^{73}≠1, θ^7≠1, hence θ primitive in F_512; D={i mod 73: θ^i∈span(1,θ)} ⊇{0,1,3,7}. (q=4 fails, matching Cohen's exception (4,3,0); all q=2^k, k≥3 work by Cohen's theorem.)

(a) in general: the problem is equivalent to finding q and z∈Z_A(F_q) with irreducible cubic and torus-generating θ^{q−1}. Examples: {0,1,4,6} gives f_z=2y^3−2y^2+2y−1, irreducible mod 3 with v_3=13 prime, so it embeds (it is itself a difference set mod 13); {0,1,3,8} gives y^3+y−1, embeds at q=5 (v=31 prime). For such sets only q prime can work and the primitivity condition is an Artin-type condition for a fixed algebraic number—conjecturally positive density of primes (plausibly provable under GRH), but I cannot prove existence of even one good prime for an arbitrary 4-element Sidon set unconditionally. So (a) is verified in all examined cases and reduced to an explicit arithmetic statement, but not fully proved in general; (b) is false in general, with {0,1,3,7} as an explicit counterexample.
